articleTitle: Exploring Wavelet Transformations for Deep Learning-Based Machine Condition Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Deep learning (DL) strategies have recently been utilized to diagnose motor faults by simply analyzing motor phase current signals, offering a less costly and non-intrusive alternative to vibration sensors. This research transforms these time-series current signals into time-frequency 2Drepresentations via Wavelet Transform (WT). The dataset for motor current signals includes 3,750 data points across five categories: one representing normal conditions and four representing artificially induced faults, each under five different load conditions: 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100%. The study employs five WT-based techniques-WT-Amor, WT-Bump, WT-Morse, WSST-Amor, and WSST-Bump. Subsequently, five DL models adopting prior Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture were developed and tested using the transformed 2D plots from each method. The DL models for WT-Amor, WT-Bump, and WT-Morse showed remarkable effectiveness with peak model accuracy of 90.93, 89.20, and 93.73%, respectively, surpassing previous 2D-image-based methods that recorded accuracy of 80.25, 74.80, and 82.80% respectively using the identical dataset and validation protocol. Notably, the WT-Morse approach slightly exceeded the formerly highest ML technique, achieving a 93.20% accuracy. However, the two WSST methods that utilized synchrosqueezing techniques faced difficulty accurately classifying motor faults. The performance of Wavelet-based deep learning methods offers a compelling alternative for machine condition monitoring.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Machine Condition Diagnosis Using Short-Time Fourier Transformation Variants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: In motor condition diagnosis, electrical current signature serves as an alternative feature to vibration-based sensor data, which is a more expensive and invasive method. Machine learning (ML) techniques have been emerging in diagnosing motor conditions using only motor phase current signals. This study converts time-series motor current signals to time-frequency 2D plots using Short-time Fourier Transform (STFT) methods. The motor current signal dataset consists of 3,750 sample points with five classes - one healthy and four synthetically-applied motor fault conditions, and with five loading conditions - 0, 25, 50, 75, and 100%. Five transformation methods are used on the dataset - non-overlap and overlap STFTs, non-overlap and overlap realigned STFTs, and synchrosqueezed STFT. Then, deep learning (DL) models based on the previous Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture are trained and validated from generated plots of each method. The DL models of overlap-STFT, overlap R-STFT, non-overlap STFT, non-overlap R-STFT, and synchrosqueezed-STFT performed exceptionally with an average accuracy of 97.65, 96.03, 96.08, 96.32, and 88.27%, respectively. Four methods outperformed the previous best ML method with 93.20% accuracy, while all five outperformed previous 2D-plot-based methods with accuracy of 80.25, 74.80, and 82.80%, respectively, using the same dataset, same DL architecture, and validation steps.

articleTitle: Estimation of Equivalent Circuit Constant of Porous Electrode by Electrochemical Impedance of Lithium Ion Battery Using Symmetrical Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The use of lithium-ion batteries (LIB) is rapidly expanding to include electric vehicles, etc., which require a high power. During sudden acceleration or rapid charging, charging and discharging are performed at a 10C rate level. As the discharge C rate increases, the apparent impedance increases, and it is difficult to derive a correct discharge curve using a linear model using measured experimental values of electrochemical impedance. We are developing an equivalent circuit model (TLM) for porous electrodes that considers the diffusion of lithium ions in the electrolyte within the porous electrode. By using this model, it is possible to simulate the relatively long response that occurs during discharge at a high C rate, as well as the short response that occurs when a pulse signal such as induced lightning strikes. To operate this circuit model, parameters for each positive electrode and negative electrode are required, which are determined theoretically or experimentally. This time, we measured the electrochemical impedance using a normal bipolar cell, and also determined the unipolar impedance of the positive and negative electrodes using a symmetrical cell and an uncharged electrode. As a result, we were able to clarify the frequency dependence of the impedance of a single positive electrode, which had been unclear until now, and estimate the ionic resistance value within the porous electrode. A similar analysis was also performed on electrodes in different charging states, and the SOC dependence of the circuit constants of each element was clarified. As a result, it became clear that the impedance decreases as the SOC increases, which is known for positive and negative bipolar cells, because the charge transfer resistance of the positive electrode decreases as the SOC increases. On the other hand, it was also found that the SOC dependence of the electric charge transfer resistance of the negative electrode is small.

articleTitle: Accelerated Life Testing for Rotating Machine Insulating Materials Exposed to High AC Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The Progressive Stress Method (PSM) and the Multi-Level Stress Method (MLM) are two crucial methodologies employed in studying the aging and failure mechanism of insulating materials subjected to high voltage stress. Each method has its pros and cons. The presented study highlights the importance of understanding the relationship between the Progressive Stress Method and the Multi-Level Stress Method in assessing the aging and failure of insulating materials. The findings revealed that for the investigated insulation material and chosen testing conditions, the aging process of insulation is remarkably similar under both stress methods. However, it is observed that at Progressive Stress Method the measured breakdown voltage is higher than in comparison with MLM. In some cases, the application of PSM leads to a shorter testing time procedure. Under certain conditions, the results obtained by PSM might be converted into MLM lifetime values which allows an effective approximation of lifetime characteristics for applied insulation materials.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of the Glass Transition Temperature of a Thermosetting Resins
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Thermosetting resins belong among the materials often used in various applications, not only in the electrical industry. The final properties of the resulting products depend on many variables that influence the curing process of the resin during its industrial production. The curing process can be evaluated based on several parameters. One of the most important is the glass transition temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>), which represents the temperature at which an amorphous polymer changes from a hard/glassy state to a soft/leathery state. Under industrial manufacturing conditions, several parameters can potentially influence this parameter. The content of this paper is aimed at determining the degree of influence of selected parameters from a particular manufacturing process. The results show that the resulting properties can depend on process factors, including the production operator, the amount of compound being prepared, the Shift, and others.

articleTitle: Robust Classification of PD Sources Using Deep Learning and Signal Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) pattern recognition technologies are highly valuable for the predictive maintenance and diagnosis of electrical insulation systems. PD signals are generated when the voltage across the cavity embedded in the insulation system exceeds the PD inception voltage. These signals are low-energy, high-frequency, and stochastic, making analysis extremely challenging since common signal processing methods cannot analyze and interpret their transient, non-stationary characteristics. It is crucial to address PD pattern recognition with a comprehensive strategy that includes collecting PD databases, feature extraction, and applying proper machine learning models. Using cutting-edge PD signal processing techniques and deep learning, PD patterns could be successfully analyzed and interpreted, resulting in the early identification of PD sources inside insulation and reducing the likelihood of system failure. The aim of the paper is to investigate and evaluate various methods to recognize partial discharge (PD) signals as single PD source (SPS) or double PD sources (DPS). Wavelet Analysis, Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), Wigner-Ville Distribution (WVD), Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), and Higher-Order Statistics (HOS) are among the techniques used, along with deep learning models.

articleTitle: What is the Effect of Salt Spray Aging on the Reliability of Conductive Joints on E-Textiles?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper deals with the reliability of conductive joints between components and textile ribbons in salty environment. In the experiment three different contacting methods (low temperature soldering, non-conductive adhesive bonding, thermocompression bonding) were used. The experiment showed that in case of non-conductive adhesive bonding method, the viscosity of adhesive is crucial and samples with high viscosity adhesive are not applicable. The experiment also showed that low temperature soldering, non-conductive adhesive bonding using a suitable non-conductive adhesive or thermocompression method with the using of a conductive filament can be recommended and joints prepared by these methods are practically applicable in salty environment.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches in Partial Discharge Modeling: Leveraging COMSOL and MATLAB for Predictive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The partial discharge technique (PD) is identified as one of the most efficient and powerful techniques for identifying the behavior of PD events in electrical power systems, particularly when studying the survival of insulation materials. For the past decade, the interpretation of partial discharge (PD) characteristics has relied predominantly on visual comparison, a method susceptible to failure due to operators lacking the requisite expertise. In the stochastic and chaotic real world, the insulation system is prone to suffer from numerous voids rather than just a single cavity, as most proposed models do, but instead is embedded with numerous voids with irregular shapes, sizes, and locations, and each one of them seems to have a different response that is undoubtedly overlapped, making it a major challenge to recognize and classify the PD sources based on their behaviors. This ability to recognize between single and multiple cavities in an insulating system becomes an important unsolved topic, emphasising the need for additional investigations. The project's goal is to develop understanding and expertise in this challenging subject through the investigation of PD events involving both single and multiple PD using the FEM PD Model.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Detection of Smallest Defects Inside Power Cable Insulation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Since the partial-discharge (PD) testing during the routine test of the cable is not able to safely detect defects in the range of 0.2mm, other testing procedures are necessary for detection. So, the hot-oil-test is performed to exclude those small defects, which can lead to breakdown of the cable after indefinite time. Unfortunately, the hot-oil-test gives only response about a short part of the produced cable length. Moreover, the measurement process is quite dependent on the experience of the employee. Hence there is a large interest to find new - in best case nondestructive - methods to find and locate small defects inside cables insulation. Former investigations focusing on ultrasonic monitoring of the cross-linking of insulation material in power cables led to the question of the minimal detectable defect size, which can be detected with ultrasonic technology. Therefore, a first study was carried out to measure defects in extruded insulation, which normally are detected by the hot-oil-test. For this article bottom holes of specified sizes down to 0.1mm were made from the inside of a medium voltage (MV) and a high voltage (HV) cross-linked poly ethylene (XLPE) cable core. Afterwards the scanning of the sample is performed. An automated micro positioning system is used, so position and depth of the defects inside the insulation layer can be exactly measured. The results of the measurements are post processed to determine the minimal detectable defect size. After analyzing the signal quality and using of different frequency filters to reduce the noise, the spectrum of the inner semicon layer (ISL) shows a valid graph with a peak at 2.1 MHz. The visualization of the defects is done with the time signal of the ultrasonic impulse (A-scan), the depth map along one axis (B-scan) and the maximum amplitude map (C-scan). The evaluation of the data showed that defects larger than 0.4 mm are clearly visible in the C-scan, which is the fastest way of visualization. Defects down to 0.1 mm are visible characteristically in the B-scan. Furthermore the theoretical minimal detectable defect size of an poly propylene (PP) flat sample is calculated.

articleTitle: On the Winding Insulation of Electrical Machines and its Aging Diagnostic Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Electrical machines are the prime mover for enormous industrial, commercial and domestic applications. These machines can be categorized on different biases: AC and DC machines according to their supply, transformers and dynamic machines such as synchronous, induction machines, and special purpose machines. Regardless of their operation working principle, they all have an essential part, which is winding. The windings in electrical machines are the main part since they are responsible on the electromagnetic field generation according to Faraday's law. Therefore, the health condition of the windings is crucial for continuous operation assurance. While it is hard to prevent electrical, thermal, mechanical, and environmental stresses, which are directly impacting the age of the windings, it is quite necessary to diagnose the insulation degradation at an early stage. Massive financial costs could be saved with the employment of a trusted diagnostic strategy. Thus, this paper aims to enlighten the recent offline and online diagnostic methods that have been used for the aforementioned purpose.

articleTitle: A Smart Way to Improving Power Quality Based on Customer Emission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The paper presents the smart approach for improving power quality. The smart approach will be based on analytical case of active filter reference determination. Active filters are used for reducing the harmonic distortion which can cause the issues on electronic power devices. The conventional approach is based on reducing all harmonic current at point of common coupling (PCC). The smart approach will be based on the customer harmonic emission which means that active filter will compensate only customer's emission. The active filter influences on the harmonic voltage distortion and the harmonic voltage distortion can be also increased. The smart approach will also have additional functionality which will not allow to increase the harmonic voltage distortion. The conventional and smart approach are tested on an analytical equivalent model. The comparison of the results will show if the size of active filter can be reduced if the smart approach is used.

articleTitle: Long-Term Stability Analysis of the Paper-Based Nomex 410 Substrate's Dielectric Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper deals with the impact of the long-term stability tests and highly-accelerated stress test on the dielectric properties of paper-based Nomex 410 substrate. The investigation of the dielectric properties of the paper-based substrate by using the split cylinder resonator Keysight 85072A under the highly accelerated stress tests in shock chamber and the long-term stability in the climatic chamber over extended periods has been carried out. The results presented in this paper contribute valuable insights to the design and optimization of electronic systems, particularly those utilizing paper-based Nomex 410 substrates, with implications for enhancing long-term stability and reliability in diverse applications.

articleTitle: Application of Transfer Learning for Instrument Transformer Condition Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Instrument transformers (ITs), namely magnetic current transformers, magnetic voltage transformers, and capacitor-coupled voltage transformers play a vital role in energy metering and reliable operation of grid protection systems. The objective of this paper is to propose an artificial intelligence based methodology for online condition monitoring of high-voltage ITs in a substation using partial discharge (PD) analysis. The methodology leverages transfer learning, i.e., utilizing a pre-trained deep learning model, fine-tuned for PD classification in ITs. The model will provide warnings and alerts regarding equipment malfunctioning based on the obtained partial discharge measurements. Moreover, the effectiveness of the methodology is validated based on laboratory experiments. Utilizing the transfer learning technique would increase the accuracy of condition-based maintenance, which will improve system reliability, ensure personnel safety, and decrease the overall maintenance cost.

articleTitle: Practical Experiences of Using FDS for Determining the Insulation Condition of Instrument Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Identifying the insulation condition of old instrument transformers in the system is crucial. Recently, high-voltage technology has been developing rapidly, primarily driven by the strong focus on the green transition of the power system. Meanwhile, manufacturers of individual transmission and distribution equipment are compelled to engage in economic optimization. To ensure optimal operation, it is important to maintain equipment throughout its lifespan to ensure reliability, safety, and economic efficiency. Effective maintenance planning necessitates regular equipment condition diagnostics. Technological progress in diagnostic equipment and measurement methods offers efficient possibilities. Dielectric frequency spectroscopy has emerged as a tool for determining electrical insulation condition, measuring impedance under variable-frequency voltage. This method allows assessing oil conductivity, moisture content, and temperature's impact on insulation. The dielectric frequency spectroscopy (FDS) method can be used on the insulation systems of various devices, this paper will present a practical application on the example of 110 kV current transformers.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Dielectric Analyses of Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) Thin Film
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: In recent years, the demands on electrical engineering materials have grown, especially regarding reliability and load capacity under increased operational stress, such as elevated temperature or voltage. Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) has emerged as a key material due to its exceptional properties under these conditions. This paper provides a detailed characterization of PEEK thin films, focusing on their electrical insulation properties and high voltage resistance. The study examines the temperature- frequency dependencies of real and imaginary part of complex relative permittivity, identifying relaxation mechanisms (α, α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>, β<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> and σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf>), and evaluates voltage endurance through time-to- failure tests under HVAC at various voltage levels (48, 56, and 64 kV/mm). Additionally, the interaction with HVDC fields is assessed using space charge analysis at voltage levels up to 50 kV/mm, confirming the presence of homo-charge, that limits the electric field strength in the vicinity of the voltage electrode.

articleTitle: Rotor Winding Diagnosis Using Sweep Frequency Response Analysis and Comparison to RSO
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Rotor windings of rotating machines are prone to high mechanical forces especially in high-speed machines and therefore often reason of unexpected failures. As the asset is a vital component in the energy generation as well as in industrial production, this can lead to high follow up costs. One major root cause are shortages between windings of a rotor pole. A reliable diagnosis of the rotor winding is therefore essential to avoid such outages. The Sweep Frequency Response Analysis (SFRA) is a highly sensitive method to perform such measurements and widely spread, especially in the world of the transformer. It was proven in several previous papers; the method can be applied as well on windings of rotating machines to check for inter-turn faults. This work targets influence factors of the measurement in practice as well as the possibility to assess the rotor winding condition reliably. To identify measurement influence factors and to identify the best frequency ranges in the SFRA measurement, 7 rotors from different machines with a rated power starting from 1,8 MVA up to 588 MVA have been investigated. On two of them, artificial short circuits between two or more windings have been implemented to investigate the sensitivity of the SFRA. Additionally, a comparison with the SFRA to the currently test implemented to detect such winding faults, the RSO (Recurrent Surge Oscillography) test was done. Having this amount of healthy and damaged windings, limits can be proposed, using a self-developed assessment algorithm. This was compared to the relative factor and the NCEPRI algorithm currently in use for transformer windings. The comparison to the Recurrent Surge Oscillography (RSO) method shows a clear advantage in sensitivity of the SFRA. Small, implemented faults where only detectable by SFRA and not with the RSO.

articleTitle: Challenges and Opportunities of Risk-Based Inspection Methods for Fire Alarm Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Risk-based approaches for the inspection of fire alarm systems offer operators and maintenance companies the opportunity to reduce both monetary and time expenditures for the operation of the systems. At the same time, the implementation of risk-based approaches for performing inspections poses challenges for those responsible. In addition to the basic classification of risks, a detailed determination of potential system vulnerabilities is required to define the depth of inspection and the inspection focus. The paper provides an overview of the most important findings with regard to risk-oriented inspection approaches for fire alarm systems and the challenges involved. A systemic approach for the successful implementation of risk-oriented inspections is presented.

articleTitle: Determination of the Level of Degradation of Generator Stator Bar Insulation Using a One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper presents the results of an experiment to classify the levels of insulation degradation of generator stator bars using a one-dimensional convolutional neural network. The stator bars were subjected to increased electrical stress during the time until insulation breakdown. The bars were periodically injected with a specially designed reference signal during the stress application to generate a dataset for training the neural network. The injected signal was acquired and then subjected to pre-processing. The paper evaluates each pre-processing variant in terms of its effect on the performance of the classification algorithm. It provides the neural network structure and its optimal parameters to accomplish the task of determining the insulation degradation state.

articleTitle: Condition Assessment of Rotating Machine Insulation: Case Studies from Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Unexpected failure of rotating machines in the power plant can cause unnecessary expense. Thus, appropriate preventive and predictive maintenance should be planned and scheduled, to avoid premature failure of the machines and to ensure the reliability and safe operation of the systems. Besides, the online monitoring technique has an advantage as it can monitor the condition periodically without interrupting the equipment and it can measure even during actual operating conditions while off-line tests can't. Indeed, the most vulnerable part of the equipment is the insulation since it is subjected to several stresses during service which can alter the insulation condition, so-called degradation. Hence, this paper intends to present the experience of insulation condition assessment on generators and motors in power plants in Thailand. Several test techniques were conducted on the machines during the annual outage including the polarization and depolarization current (PDC) analysis, off-line partial discharge (PD) test as well as dissipation factor and capacitance tip-up. Those diagnostic test techniques are useful as effective tools to evaluate the insulation condition of the machines. The experimental results will be introduced and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of 3D Printed Layered Insulation Consisting of PET-G and TPE Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper investigates the suitability of 3D-printed dielectric insulation composed of PET-G (Polyethylene Tereph-thalate Glycol) and TPE (Thermoplastic Elastomer) materials, focusing on their performance as an insulation in DC (Direct current) applications. For this goal, several diagnostic methods were employed, including dissipation factor measurement, dielectric strength testing, broadband dielectric spectroscopy, volume resistivity measurement, and the Pulse Electro-Acoustic (PEA) method, to evaluate the electrical properties and reliability of such insulation material. The addition of a TPE layer over the PET-G base material is considered as a way to enhance abrasion resistance while maintaining the dielectric properties. However, challenges related to space charge accumulation and its impact on long-term performance, particularly under DC conditions, are considered, as the nature of 3D printed parts strongly support space charge accumulation under DC electric field.

articleTitle: Practical Experience with PD-Localization in Rotating Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper deals with the topic of localization within spatial distributed windings, such as is rotating machines and transformers, and is a follow up to the work we presented at the 2022 CDEE. Given are two case studies of rotating machines with high PD-level, on which PD-localization is conducted. The localization method is explained briefly and challenges compared to the classic TDR-evaluation, which is performed at cables, are discussed. The localization results on the two stators are discussed in detail and also put in context to the related PRPD-pattern. Finally, recommendations are proposed after assessment based on the measurements.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Using Polyethylene Carbon Material AF-1361 for Sensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Recent advancements in polymer composite development have paved the way for cost-effective solutions in flexible tactile and pressure sensors. This paper explores the potential of a polyethylene-carbon composite material, specifically AF-1361, for flexible sensor design. The study focuses on analyzing the material's behavior regarding resistivity changes induced by external forces, particularly investigating the roles of percolation phenomena and quantum tunneling. Additionally, the research examines changes in the resistance of flexible sensors in response to various magnitudes of applied force. The insights obtained from this study contribute to understanding the potential applications of AF-1361 in sensor technology and highlight its effectiveness in fabricating flexible sensors.

articleTitle: The Influence of Nitrogen Atmosphere on Properties and Development of IMCs in Selected Lead-Free Solders
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of different atmospheric conditions and plasma treatment on the wetting properties and intermetallic compound (IMC) thickness in lead-free soldering processes. Lead-free solders, primarily composed of high tin content, exhibit different wetting characteristics compared to traditional lead-based solders, influencing the quality and durability of solder joints. The use of an inert nitrogen atmosphere during soldering significantly improved wetting quality, reducing oxidation and enhancing solder flow. Plasma treatment further increased the wetted surface area by an average of 10%. The analysis also highlighted that thermal profiles had a more substantial effect on wetting quality and IMC properties than atmospheric conditions. Under nitrogen, IMC thickness remained stable across thermal profiles, while vacuum conditions showed increased IMC thickness and variability with high profile settings. These findings suggest that optimizing atmospheric conditions and thermal profiles is crucial for improving solder joint reliability in lead-free soldering, with plasma treatment showing potential as an additional enhancement technique. Future research will explore varying plasma treatment settings to further optimize solder joint quality.

articleTitle: Polarization and Electric Field Distribution of Stacked Dielectrics at Transient Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Electric components are facing new challenges due to modern electronic power supplies used for renewable energies and electric vehicles. Understanding the behavior of material combinations and the resulting field distribution at non-sinusoidal voltage excitation is necessary to design and optimize reliable insulating systems. This study presents a measurement setup to test the polarization models obtained from broadband dielectric spectroscopy measurements against measurements at transient excitation. The frequency and temperature dependent polarization models can be used for circuit simulations containing polarizing capacitors and field simulations at arbitrary waveforms.

articleTitle: Polyethylene-based Composites with a Three-Component Inorganic Flame Retardant - Effect of a Different Component Ratio on Dielectric and Mechanical Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The polymer composites based on polyethylene (PE) with particulate filler enhancing flame retardancy are increasingly used in producing cable insulation layers, even the most electrically stressed core insulation. This study evaluates the effect of flame retardants based on the commonly used aluminium hydroxide (ATH), magnesium hydroxide (MDH), and still less common but promising clay mineral called halloysite nanotubes (HNT) on the dielectric and mechanical properties of the PE composites designed primarily for the cable core insulation. The aim of the production of composites with mentioned fillers is to improve flame retardancy and to affect the dielectric and mechanical properties as little as possible compared to the neat PE by varying the proportions of fillers. Based on previous research, the total weight proportion of fillers in PE has always been 5%. Specifically, this study evaluates the effects of four different filler ratios on selected dielectric characteristics (relative permittivity, dissipation factor, dielectric strength, and volume resistivity) and the results of tensile tests. The results indicate an increase in dissipation factor with adding the filler, particularly with the combination of ATH:MDH:HNT in a 1:1:3 ratio. The dielectric strength remained consistent, except for the ratio of 3:1:1, which showed improvement. The mechanical properties were minimally affected, with the ratio of 1:1:3 exhibiting notable changes. The optimisation of the ratio of fillers incorporated primarily in terms of their fire retardancy of PE is also not negligible concerning dielectric and mechanical properties.

articleTitle: Optimizing Simulation Model for Portraying the Effect of Direct Lightning Strike to Ground with Regard to MV Cable Outer Sheath
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Over the past twenty years, there have been numerous instances of damage to the outer sheath of cables, the cause of which remains unknown. Surprisingly, some of these cables were not even in use at the time of the incidents. Most of the damages occurred in areas with a high frequency of lightning strikes. To address this issue, a research study is currently underway to examine the impact of direct lightning strikes on medium voltage cables and develop protective measures. As part of the study that is ongoing, we are developing a simulation model that takes into account factors such as soil ionization, lightning parameters, and moisture to mimic realistic lightning strikes on the ground. The main aim is to utilize the acquired knowledge to aid in selecting suitable cable design for future projects.

articleTitle: Comparative Investigation at AC-Arcing vs. DC-Arcing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: DC applications are becoming increasingly widespread. As a result, the number of arc flash events in such systems will increase. To ensure an appropriate system and personal protection, it is important to know occurring arc effects and suitable methods for protecting against the effects of a gas discharge. While studies so far only focused on AC networks, there is currently little reliable information available regarding arc faults with DC. For this reason, extensive LV DC investigations carried out in the IPH Berlin. As a result, different effects could be determined, which were elevated with regard to a risk assessment. In addition, a conventional (AC) active protection system was integrated into a DC voltage application, to check whether this method is also possible at DC level. This paper summarizes the most important findings with the aim of establishing a comparison of both forms of electrical voltage while arcing is coming up.

articleTitle: Measurement of Ultrasonic Emissions on Stator Winding of Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper is focused on the measurement of ultrasonic emissions on complete stator windings in different stage of operation life. New approach “cuts” the winding to individual parts which are investigated, and results are then connected again to comprehensive winding chart. We can track the measured parameters trends more thoroughly and see weak spots.

articleTitle: Characterization of Nitride Nanoparticles and the Properties of Nitride Dielectric Nanofluid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Dielectric and thermal properties of natural ester oil can be enhanced using specific nanoparticles. Nitride nanoparticles have been selected due to their promising thermal properties. Aluminium nitride, Hexagonal boron nitride, and Silicon nitride nanoparticles were incorporated into rapeseed oil at a weight fraction of 0.25%. The preparation of the nanofluid itself is described and selected nanoparticles were characterized using Simultaneous thermal analysis and Fast Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. The breakdown voltage, dissipation factor, relative permittivity, and internal resistivity were measured. Dissipation factor and relative permittivity have been measured as a function of temperature (30°C to 90°C) at 50 Hz and 500 V. Subsequently, the aforementioned parameters were evaluated, and the overall experimental procedure was assessed.

articleTitle: The Probability-Based Model of an Electric Discharge Growth
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The analysis of the electric resilience of an insulating material is mainly the subject of experiments. However, with an increase in computing power, numerical simulations are more and more preferred as an alternative approach to the experimental and empirical efforts. Compared to the experiments, the numerical simulations are less demanding in terms of time and expenditures, but at the cost of the necessity to understand physical processes and their correct implementation into a numerical model itself. This article deals with the simplification of the physical processes of discharge phenomena and their implementation into the numerical model applicable for commercial purposes.

articleTitle: Dielectric Analysis of Silicone Gels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Given the dynamic development of power electronics and semiconductors, it's essential to innovate materials capable of withstanding high electric field intensities and partial discharges. Silicone gels are part of a group of potting compounds used as the main insulation system for power devices. Due to the continuous development of power devices and increasing levels of operating voltages, issues arise concerning partial discharges at the interface substrate-gel-conductor. This interface is well known as the triple point, where a significant increase in electric field intensity occurs. This paper presents a structural analysis of silicone gel commonly used as the main insulation in these applications to observe structural changes and dielectric properties.

articleTitle: Identification and Characterization of Modulation Scheme in an EV-PMSM Control Strategy for Digital Twin Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Digital twins (DT), virtual replicas of physical systems, play a pivotal role in design, monitoring, and optimization across various industries. However, the accuracy of DT relies heavily on the precision of their underlying virtual models, presenting a challenge when physical system parameters are not fully known. This research addresses this challenge by proposing a comprehensive approach to identify and characterize the modulation scheme employed in the control strategy of an Electric Vehicle Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (EV-PMSM). The proposed algorithm utilizes actual stator voltage and current signals obtained from the EV motor drive test bench. The identification process involves three sequential steps: switching frequency calculation, spectrum analysis, and harmonic analysis. The results of this analysis strongly indicate the utilization of Space Vector Modulation (SVM) in the control strategy. Finally, the voltage vector distribution (VVD) was calculated to serve as a cornerstone for the precise modeling of the modulator.

articleTitle: Overview of Dielectric Properties of Epoxy-glass-mica Layered Composites with Incorporated Polymeric Films
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper proposes an addition of polymeric film layers into a conventional high-voltage insulating composite. The effects of the addition of such fourth component to a standard three-component composite are assessed. Tested specimens were prepared as thin sheets of conventional prepregs with fibre reinforcement to which separate polymeric films were added. The first type of prepared composites consisted only of three-component prepregs and was the reference material. The other three prepared composites consisted of prepregs with incorporated polymeric films of polyimide (PI), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyethylene naphthalate (PEN). Volume resistivity, relative permittivity, loss factor, and partial discharge activity were measured on the press-cured specimens of layered composites. The measurement results were compared between the reference and composites incorporating different polymeric films. The results indicate that the primary differences between reference and composites with polymeric films are in the volume resistivity and dissipation factor. Analysis of partial discharge activity reveals varying behaviour between tested composites based on phase-resolved partial discharge patterns.

articleTitle: Effects of MgO Nanoparticles on Viscoelastic Properties of Linear Low-Density Polyethylene
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Linear Low-Density Polyethylene (LLDPE) is a semicrystalline polymer with potential for use in High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmissions. Its mechanical and electrical insulating properties can be improved by addition of nanofillers to the pure LLDPE matrix. This paper deals with the influence of magnesium oxide nanoparticles (MgO) with content from 0 to 10 wt. % on the viscoelastic properties of LLDPE. The reinforcing effect as a result of immobilization of the polymer chains on the filler surface after incorporation of MgO nanoparticles was deduced from analysis of DMA measurements. Three relaxation processes associated with chain motion in amorphous, interfacial and crystalline regions were identified in the temperature dependence of loss modulus and damping factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$tan\delta$</tex> in all studied samples. Temperatures associated with the first two processes were slightly influenced by the presence of MgO nanoparticles, in contrast to the third one, in which a more significant shift to higher temperatures was observed in comparison to pure LLDPE.

articleTitle: Low Power Measurement of Low Resistances by Simple Lock-In Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The paper is focused on unconventional low power method of measurement of very low resistances by means of a lock-in amplifier. There is explained the principle of a lock-in amplifier, design and implementation of simple lock-in amplifier with AD630 integrated circuit and implementation of a special shielded measuring chamber for sample connection as well. Subsequently, calibration process of the measuring system and comparative measurement on several samples of low value resistors is described. The results reveal ability to measure very low resistances by means of currents values that are many orders lower than in case of standard DC Ohm´s law method.

articleTitle: Investigation of Thermal Conductivity Coefficient in Polyurethane Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The study aims to explore the influence of varying nanoparticle content on the thermal conductivity coefficient of polyurethane composites. The setup employs conventional laboratory instruments, including a current source and a 16-channel digitizer, with LabVIEW automation for measurements. The research involves an analysis of few methods employed to measure thermal conductivity. The investigation specifically focuses on the incorporation of nanoparticles to tailor the thermal conductivity of polyurethane and presents comparison between various nanoparticle content levels. The preparation of samples follows established protocols, ensuring homogeneity and reproducibility. The study concludes by discussing the methodology, results, and potential enhancements to the experimental configuration.

articleTitle: Modeling of Electrical Insulation System of Turbogenerators with a Higher Value of Coefficient of Thermal Conductivity and Associated Ecological Perspectives and Economic Benefit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: New technologies, production of electricity, and energy savings play a significant role in the rise of the economic potential of each country and have a significant impact on the environment. The growing demand for electrical energy and the use of turbogenerators in electricity production have led to their irreplaceable role. History shows that at the end of the 20th century and at the beginning of the 21st century usable energy from fossil fuels is running out, and renewable energies are still not developed enough to offer a full replacement. Therefore, any attempt to improve the quality of turbogenerators is of considerable value. Electrical insulation systems (EIS) of turbogenerators have been developed and optimized during the last 60 years. This article discusses how to improve the removal of heat from electrical insulation systems and at the same time increase the performance of high-voltage electrical equipment thereby reducing weight and reducing their dimensions by increasing the value of the coefficient of thermal conductivity of electrical insulation systems. An increase in thermal conductivity can be achieved by adding a filler with a higher thermal conductivity coefficient to electrical insulation systems. By modeling the distribution of the temperature field with a change in the coefficient of thermal conductivity, the assumption that fillers can affect the thermal properties of the electrical insulation system was verified. The economic benefit of an electrical insulation system with a higher value of the thermal conductivity coefficient is stated at the end of this article.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Basic Electrical Insulation Properties of the Two-Component System Using by Several Diagnostic Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: In this study, the effect of 2.0, respectively 5.0 weight percent filler of halloysite (HNT) dopant for dielectric properties of two two-component polyurethane potting agent were studied. In this study, polyurethane-based potting compounds from VUKI a.s. were used as the base medium, one being a pure potting compound with the factory name VUKOL N22 and the second potting compound having the designation VUKOL N22u Magna Blue. For this purpose, direct volume resistivity measurements and broadband dielectric spectroscopy measurements were used to describe changes in the dielectric responses of the studied nanocomposites doped with HNT. The investigation of the dependence of complex relative permittivity and dissipation factor was conducted using dielectric frequency spectroscopy within a temperature range of 25°C to 120°C and a frequency range of 1 mHz to 1 MHz. The measurements of resistance were carried out following the standard STN 34 6460: 1993, with the ambient temperature consistently maintained at 25°C.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Measurement at Pulse Voltage: Design of a Measurement Circuit and its Components
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Renewable Energies and electric vehicles rely on semiconductor switches. The switching pulses generated by such are found to accelerate the ageing process of dielectrics and possibly triggering partial discharges. Partial discharge measurement has developed to an established tool for quality assurance and failure identification at alternating voltages and is being continuously researched. The aim of this paper is to present a measurement circuit suitable to perform direct partial discharge measurements at pulse voltage excitation and accessing the partial discharge quantities known from conventional PD measurements following IEC 60270.

articleTitle: Long Term Diagnostic Experience in Measuring and Evaluating Leakage Current for 110 kV Surge Arresters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Number of surge arresters in the electric power system are increasing rapidly. A device for testing ZnO surge arresters was designed based on spectral analysis. Through this method, we can determine the frequency content of the first and third harmonic frequencies, which can then be used to estimate the condition of the surge arrester based on the leakage current. The benefit of measurement is that you can test the arresters while they are operating. Testing in the field may not be possible consistently due to the diverse grounding configurations and arrester installations. In these circumstances, the arrester must be tested in the laboratory. Another advantage of testing, based on harmonic analysis of the leakage current from the arrester in a steady state is that detailed factory data, which may not always be available due to the many different types of surge arresters, are not required. The significance of surge arrester testing over the years has been highlighted, as faults in surge arresters have a significant impact on operational reliability of electric power system. The article will stress the significance of keeping track of the condition evaluation of surge arresters and the importance of the diagnostic method.

articleTitle: Adequacy of Dielectric-Based Deducted Quantities as an Aging Indicator in EPR/CSPE Low Voltage Cables in Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Radiation can significantly affect the aging of cables in nuclear power plants. The exposure of cables to radiation, such as gamma rays, neutrons, and other forms of ionizing radiation, can lead to the degradation of their materials over time. This degradation can manifest in various ways, including changes in mechanical properties, electrical characteristics, and overall structural integrity. The effect of nuclear radiation on the EPR/CSPE power cables was investigated where the cable samples were exposed to a specific radiation dose rate of 0.8 kGy/h during multiple periods to mimic the aging process in the nuclear power plant. The change after the long-term nuclear radiation exposure was assessed and studied by electrical (dielectric spectrum parameter measurement) and mechanical Elongation at Break (EaB) methods. Having both the loss factor values and the corresponding capacitance throughout the frequency spectrum, eight deducted values were correlated with the elongation at break set of values to examine their adequacy as a possible ageing predictor. It was found that some of these values have a clear correlation with the EaB which can be considered as an indicator for the radiation degradation process.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Effect of Different Radiation Dose Rates on the Electrical Properties of EPR-Insulated I&C Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This study investigates the electrical behavior of Ethylene Propylene Rubber (EPR) insulation used in instrumentation and control (I&C) cables in nuclear power plants (NPPs). Cables were subjected to different accelerated radiation aging dose rates, 100 Gy/h and 800 Gy/h respectively. After aging, dissipation factor (tanδ) trend with frequency from 500 Hz to 500 kHz was obtained. Results show that tanδ of the higher dose rates depicts a faster increase than the lower one, following the aging severity. In particular, the tanδ trend at high frequencies (greater than 100 kHz) shows a linear increase with aging for both dose rates, proposing it as a suitable radiation aging marker for EPR materials.

articleTitle: Durability of New Developed PCB Surface Finishes to Multiple Reflow
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The article investigates the durability of newly developed printed circuit board (PCB) surface finishes in the context of multiple reflow processes. A PCB's surface finish is crucial for ensuring robust and reliable solder connections, which are essential for long-lasting performance. In the absence of a suitable finish, solder adhesion may be compromised, leading to weak joints and potential failures. PCBs are required to consistently perform over extended periods, often undergoing multiple reflow cycles in the case of double-sided boards. Different finish types exhibit unique properties, advantages, and challenges, influencing the board's overall performance, longevity, and reliability. This article addresses the challenges associated with evaluating solder wettability and the contact angle of molten solder balls. A detailed comparison is made between established finishes such as ENIG, Cu, ImSn, and newly developed surface finishes (SnAg7, SnAg7DOC, SnAg5, SnAg5ENi). Wettability is assessed using a self-developed laboratory device that allows for in-situ measurements of the contact angle. Experimental results indicate a decrease in wettability for some surface finishes. The newly developed SnAg7-based surface finish is highlighted for its excellent solderability and flat surface, making it suitable for various applications, including those requiring multiple reflow processes.

articleTitle: Dielectric and Mechanical Response of Cold-Curing Epoxy Resin to Hygrothermal Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The electrical insulation system plays a pivotal role in the design and operation of electric machines. It is important and it might be crucial to describe the material aging process and subsequently monitor the acting ambient degradation factors as these systems are always exposed to these factors to some extent. Epoxy resin is a typical material used in the electrical insulating systems of rotating electrical machines at various voltage and power ratings. Therefore, epoxy resin is the investigated material in this study. This paper aims to describe the aging process and the material response to the harsh experiment setup of multifactor hygrothermal stress. The results in this study report a decline in all investigated parameters of the specimens including both the dielectric and mechanical properties. It appears that mechanical properties are slightly more suitable for the aging process description even after longer expositions and near-completed saturation. Collected data are further discussed in this study.

articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation of Ageing Phenomena of Low-Voltage and High-Voltage High-Rupture Capacity Fuses due to Longterm Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The paper presents analyses on low-voltage and high-voltage AC fuses with the aim of examining their state of ageing at the end of their service time. The test sample consisted of about 180 LV fuses and 20 HV back-up fuses, all of them aged 35 and over. Investigations were made on their optical condition, resistances, time-current characteristics, thermal behav-iour and switching behaviour in the range of their minimum to their maximum breaking current. It was found that the behav-iour of the samples studied differs, sometimes considerably, from the nominal behaviour of as-new fuses which is defined by recognised state-of-the-art type tests ([1], [2], [3] et al.). The dis-crepancy between nominal and observed behaviour is traced to deterioration.

articleTitle: The Influence of Frequency Range on VLF Partial Discharge measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Testing at very low frequencies (typically 0,1 Hz and less) represents an alternative to DC, 50 or 60 Hz hipot tests. It is standardized and up-to date method for medium voltage cable condition assessment. VLF tests can be also used for partial discharge detection and measurement. Unlike the partial discharge detection at power grid frequency, partial discharges at VLF testing have different characteristics and parameters. Furthermore, the possibility of partial discharge detection in various frequency ranges makes the situation even more complicated. Various frequency ranges sometimes provide various results from a single device under the test.

articleTitle: Online Fault Localization on Offshore Wind Farm Inter-Array Cable via Deconvolution-Based Fault Signal Restoration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: With growing demands of offshore wind energy, condition assessment of power infrastructures in offshore wind farms becomes crucial. Among the electrical equipment, diagnostics of inter-array cables is essential owing to its role of interconnecting between the facilities and power transmission. In this paper, we propose a new online fault localization algorithm that locates a failure of cable by applying deconvolution to acquired signals considering the propagation characteristics of the cable. When propagated fault signals are acquired by the time-synchronized fault recorders located at both ends of the cable, the fault signals are restored in both directions for each unit distance based on the estimated cable transfer function. After the process of pairing the bidirectionally restored signal with the signal on the same point, the similarity between each paired signal is measured by normalized cross-correlation. Finally, the fault location is estimated from the point with the highest similarity. In order to verify the robustness of the proposed method, experiments estimating various locations of faults are conducted, and failure scenarios are emulated at every unit distance using a computational simulation tool. We expect that the proposed method can improve the reliability of system operation on wind farm.

articleTitle: Transferability of SFRA Measurements Between Rotating Machines of Different Power Class and Type
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Diagnostic methods are important in the operation of rotating machines in power generation or industry. This study investigates the application of the sweep-frequency-response-analysis (SFRA) for rotating machines. It uses the frequency response of the device under test for fault detection. Machines of large power classes are rarely accessible for research, which is why often small laboratory machines are used for detailed investigations to gain a profound understanding of the basic behavior of rotating machines. This work focuses on the transferability between laboratory machines and machines in practical operation. The most significant difference is the power class with corresponding larger geometric dimensions. Another crucial factor is the number of pole pairs, which describes the construction of the machine. Nevertheless, equal fundamental response characteristics apply for all machines, and this investigation shows which frequency range shifts are caused by which characteristic. This is an essential factor for transferability. To verify the correlations, various constructions and types of machines are analyzed based on power class and number of pole pairs. Measurements on hydro-generators and turbo runners are presented and compared. Hydro-generators are characterized by their low speed due to the high number of pole pairs. Their unique structural design, with a short rotor length but a large diameter, differs strongly from turbo runners or salient-pole machines with lower pole number. Furthermore, induction motors of both smaller and larger power classes are compared, considering different numbers of pole pairs. In conclusion, the defined frequency ranges, low-pass, local maximum, and main resonance, indicate more or less distinct dependencies on the number of pole pairs and power class. The double resonance shows no correlation among the examined test objects. The characteristics are consistently transferable, proving the possibility of transferring findings from laboratory machines to industrial motors and generators.

articleTitle: Comparative Vibration Response Analysis of 3-Phase and 9-Phase PMSM Prototype
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The multiphase machines have become an object of interest to many researchers and engineers as they offer significantly higher reliability since they are less prone to high vibration levels after a one-phase disconnection fault. Moreover, multiphase machines provide less vibration due to the smooth waveform of the magnetomotive force. This study aims to characterize and perform the comparative analysis of 3-phase and 9-phase PMSM prototypes strictly in terms of phase disconnecting faulty operational regimes. The paper describes the designed condition monitoring and diagnostic system used for data acquisition. The investigation confirms the hypothesis on lower vibration levels during a one-phase disconnection fault. The results also include a spectral and RMS values comparison and a discussion of both 3-phase and 9-phase machine vibrations in various combinations of faulty regimes.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Q(U) Curve and Flexibility on the Integration of PVs in a Low-Voltage Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: As the integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into low-voltage distribution networks continues to rise, understanding the impact of their Q(U) characteristics or active power set-point flexibility is becoming increasingly important. This paper explores the correlation between the generated energy and the Q(U) curve of PVs and between the generated energy and flexibility while ensuring that the grid operates within voltage limits. The study emphasizes the need for a comprehensive understanding of PV system behaviors to ensure the effective management of network stability and reliability. A case study conducted in a low voltage network demo, where the flexibility market is investigated, is presented. The case study delves into the dynamic interaction between PV systems and the distribution network, shedding light on the challenges and opportunities associated with integrating flexibility mechanisms.

articleTitle: Fundamental Introduction of a Holistic Modeling Approach Enabling the Depiction of Sector-Coupled Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This publication showcases the sector-specific transformations associated with the energy transition and the strive for carbon neutrality in Germany. The interconnectedness of sector-coupled energy systems and the necessity for simulations capable of modeling the behavior of such systems is emphasized. The fundamentals of a state-space based modeling approach applicable for steady-state and transient analysis are introduced. Its application for the holistic calculation of sector-coupled energy systems relying on sector-specific equivalent circuit diagrams is presented.

articleTitle: Application of Education Models for the Concept of Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Industry 4.0 integrates advanced technologies, digitization, and automation into traditional industrial environments to maximize efficiency and competitiveness in manufacturing enterprises. This concept connects physical manufacturing systems with digital technologies by implementing technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), advanced robotics, and artificial intelligence (AI). The realization of these goals requires qualified personnel who must be equipped with the necessary technical knowledge and practical skills. For these technologies to be used effectively, it is necessary to train students properly. One of the innovative approaches to teaching the principles of Industry 4.0 is the use of modular models and kits that allow the simulation of real production situations without the risk of operational errors. These models often include advanced technologies such as virtual reality (VR) or augmented reality (AR) to create realistic environments for simulating complex processes. As part of this approach, an automated production line to assemble LEGO cars was developed. This long-term project uses LEGO Technics as the construction platform and LEGO Mindstorms to control electronics and software. Its main goal is to develop a comprehensive educational system per OECD recommendations for teaching Industry 4.0 concepts. This educational system enables the simulation of various types of problems that may occur on the production line (mechanical, electrical, process-related) and in the operational software, providing a comprehensive platform for practicing solving real manufacturing scenarios.

articleTitle: Frequency Response Analysis on Rotating Machines – Model Parameterization for Different Machine Types and Performance Classes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Synchronous and induction machines are essential in power technology and industry. Therefore, their reliable operation and low failure rate are of high importance. Frequency Response Analysis (FRA) shows promising potential as a diagnostic method for rotating machines. Previous studies have shown the ability to detect various faults with relatively low effort. This paper investigates the influence of individual machine parameters on the frequency response of rotating machines, using simulations of a grey box model. These parameters are calculated based on pre-defined characteristic frequency points or determined iteratively, with the aim to fundamentally replicate the characteristics from measurements in order to describe essential electrical and magnetic properties. For this purpose, a novel method for parameterization is introduced. The frequency response is divided into defined frequency ranges: the low-pass behaviour, the double resonance, the local maximum, and the main resonance. Corresponding parameters are then sequentially determined, either by calculation or iteratively. The results are verified by an analysis of a fault-free synchronous machine. It shows that the simulation already provides a solid representation of the measurement results. By utilizing the Standard Deviation of Difference (SDD) for evaluation, the deviation between measurement and simulation is analyzed. The assessment demonstrates a close correlation with the measured behaviour. However, varying degrees of deviation occur depending on the frequency range. The synchronous machine examined in this paper exhibits a close approximation with an SDD of up to 5 dB for the low-pass behaviour and the double resonance. As for the parameterization of the local maximum and the main resonance, the SDD reaches up to 20 dB. Noticeably larger deviations occur at frequencies beyond the main resonance. The reasons behind these larger deviations are explained, and their relevance within this frequency range is illustrated.

articleTitle: High Voltage Circuit Breaker Charging Motor's Condition Monitoring – Importance, Possibilities, and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The reliable operation of high voltage circuit breakers (HVCB), their unfailing control and monitoring from remote locations is becoming increasingly significant day by day as the world is moving towards Internet of Things (IoT) and other industry 4.0 standards. Among other parts of HVCB, the spring charging motor (SCM) plays a very crucial role by keeping the HVCB ready for operation without manual interference. The failing of SCM may start the cascading faults in the power network by ending the possibility of its control from remote locations. Hence the continuous health monitoring of SCM for control and predictive maintenance is of paramount importance. This paper provides a comprehensive overview on the possible faults of SCM, the importance of their detection at incipient stage, an insight into the future of the advanced fault detection techniques and their implementation challenges.

articleTitle: Digital Predictive Maintenance: Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper deals with the issue of digital predictive maintenance and its application to selected equipment, focusing on a case study of climate chambers. The study analyzed the current state of maintenance of these devices, performed cost calculations, and evaluated the possible risks. Based on these analyses, a procedure for the implementation of predictive maintenance was proposed, which could lead to the reduction of the identified risks and the optimization of the costs associated with the maintenance of the equipment. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of digital predictive maintenance that includes a theoretical framework, a case study, and an implementation methodology, thus contributing to a deeper understanding of the benefits and challenges associated with this area.
